name: Orbit AI - Phase 1 - Portal e-sign submitted

nodes.name: Portal e-sign webhook
nodes.notes: Replaces the old Documenso-webhook-based version of this workflow (brief v2: MVP e-sign is a lightweight inline capture on the Proposal page itself - typed name + checkbox + timestamp + IP - not a third-party e-sign vendor; Documenso is now an optional later upgrade, not an MVP dependency). ASSUMPTION: the portal (a Netlify-hosted client-facing site, not built in this repo) posts here directly rather than writing to Twenty CRM itself - consistent with the brief's 'dialer + Demo Dashboard + Deals Desk all write through n8n as a single choke point' pattern, extended to the portal for the same reason, but not explicitly stated for this specific write. responseMode is 'responseNode' (not 'onReceived' like the other Phase 1 webhooks) because the portal's own JS needs a synchronous success/fail response before it unlocks the Onboarding Form step.

nodes.name: Valid signature payload?
nodes.notes: Minimal server-side defense against a malformed/tampered request - real validation (does opportunityId correspond to a real, not-already-signed Opportunity) would need a Twenty CRM read first, not built here to keep this workflow's first draft simple. IP address itself isn't validated here - it's just recorded (see the next node), trusted from the portal's request as the client's IP. If the portal sits behind a proxy/CDN (Netlify does), confirm the portal captures the real client IP (X-Forwarded-For) rather than an edge IP before this data is treated as a real audit-trail record.

nodes.name: Advance CRM to Contract Signed

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ stage: 'Contract Signed', esignTypedName: $json.body.typedName, esignTimestamp: $json.body.timestampIso, esignIp: $json.body.ip }) }}

nodes.notes: Writes the signature's own fields (typed name, timestamp, IP) directly onto the Opportunity - unlike the research/audit content in the lead-intake workflow, this doesn't violate the Opportunity Card 'no embedded live data' principle, since a signature record IS the CRM-native fact being tracked here, not a rendering of some other tool's content. Same Twenty CRM REST-shape uncertainty as every other workflow in this library.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: false, reason: 'Missing or invalid signature fields (typedName, checked, opportunityId all required).' }) }}
